declared_hypothesis: Deterrence of legitimate pollinator use by a flower-associated chemical barrier is concentrated at concentrations above the range reported for the focal system; within the reported natural range the oriented route effect attenuates toward zero or reverses.
licensed_statement: Whether the sign of the realised D -> pollinator-use route depends on declared dose realism.
interpretation: Primary context test. A level reversal shows that the constituent pathway feeding mutualist interference is not a fixed constant of the trait label.

declared_hypothesis: The oriented route effect becomes more negative as the manipulated concentration rises relative to the maximum concentration reported for the focal system.
licensed_statement: Whether the realised D -> pollinator-use route effect varies monotonically with declared relative dose.
interpretation: Continuous form of the dose-realism test; retains studies whose reported concentrations do not fall cleanly into two declared classes.

declared_hypothesis: Paired-choice laboratory assays return a more negative oriented route effect than free-foraging field assays of the same trait class.
licensed_statement: Whether the measured route effect depends on the declared assay context rather than on the trait alone.
interpretation: Design-context test. A significant contrast constrains how laboratory deterrence thresholds may be transferred to a field pollination channel.

declared_hypothesis: The oriented route effect differs between social bees and other legitimate flower visitors.
licensed_statement: Whether the measured route effect depends on the declared pollinator functional group.
interpretation: Exploratory context test. Declared before extraction so that a null result remains reportable.
